title: Brera to Moreno 2091: the Milanese who gave Buenos Aires its liberty facades
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: Brera, Milan: the birth
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia, 'Virginio Colombo', gives 22 July 1884 in the Brera district of Milan. it.wikipedia gives only the year 1885, with no day and no month, so the day and month rest on the Spanish edition alone and the two editions contradict each other on the year; the contradiction is not resolved here. es.wikipedia is also inconsistent with itself: a 22 July 1884 birth against its own 22 July 1927 death yields 43 years, while its text reads 'falleció a la temprana edad de 42 años'. Both editions print 42.
stops.campa: A son is born in Brera, the quarter of the academy, where Lombard architecture has been taught for a hundred years and where the boy will be taught it in his turn. Milan around him is the capital of Italian liberty: iron, cement, wet drapery and vegetation carved onto the fronts of apartment houses built for a bourgeoisie with new money and an appetite for being looked at. He will spend his working life doing that same thing in Buenos Aires, for clients with the same appetite. The date es.wikipedia gives for the birth is 22 July 1884; the Italian edition gives 1885, with no day and no month at all.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia, 'Virginio Colombo', birth entry (22 July 1884, Brera)
it.wikipedia, 'Virginio Colombo', which gives 1885 with no day or month

stops.name: Accademia di Belle Arti di Brera: the master
stops.date_confidence: Neither Wikipedia edition dates the training at all; the years c.1900-1905 come only from the self-published virginiocolombo.blogspot.com, which also supplies the Camillo Boito detail, so the whole dating of this stop is reconstruction [R]. The date shown defaults to 1 January of a midpoint year and carries no evidentiary weight. Giuseppe Sommaruga as his master is attested by both editions [A]. it.wikipedia additionally lists Antonio Sant'Elia as a teacher; that is impossible and is excluded here, since Sant'Elia was born in 1888, reached Milan only in 1907 and enrolled at Brera in 1909, three years after Colombo had sailed.
stops.campa: He studies architecture at the Accademia di Belle Arti di Brera and becomes a student of Giuseppe Sommaruga, the leading figure of Milanese liberty, whose fronts treat ornament as structure rather than as icing on it. No document reached here fixes the years he sat in that courtyard, or names a single drawing he made in it. What he took from the man is legible only later, in Buenos Aires, on streets Sommaruga never sees: mass first, then a swarm of modelled figures pushed out of the wall until the wall reads as sculpture.
suggested_refs: Giuseppe Sommaruga's Milanese liberty work, the direct model for Colombo's Buenos Aires facades

stops.name: Genoa: the passage for the River Plate
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction [R]. No source names Colombo's port of departure, his ship, or the month of the crossing; only the year of arrival, 1906, is attested by es.wikipedia. Genoa is the standard embarkation point for northern Italian emigrants to the River Plate in this period and the pin is the one already fixed for that route. The two fellow travellers are reported only by virginiocolombo.blogspot.com and are uncorroborated.
stops.campa: Nothing in the record puts him on a particular ship or a particular quay. What is known is that in 1906 a young Milanese with an academy training and no built work of his own is in Buenos Aires under contract to the Argentine Ministry of Public Works, and that men like him left from Genoa, three weeks of Atlantic and a call at Montevideo. Two others are said to travel with him and matter later: Achille de Lázzari and Mario Baroffio Covati, hired for the same job in the same drafting rooms.
suggested_refs: Genoa as the embarkation port for northern Italian crossings to the River Plate, 1900-1914

stops.name: Palacio de Justicia, Talcahuano 550: the contract for the decorations
stops.date_confidence: The 1906 arrival and the Ministry of Public Works contract for decorative work on the Palacio de Justicia are attested by es.wikipedia [A], which gives no month; the date defaults to 1 January. The coordinate is the Palacio de Justicia itself, at Talcahuano 550, San Nicolás, per OpenStreetMap and the es.wikipedia infobox reading 34 36 08 S, 58 23 09 W.
stops.campa: The Ministry of Public Works has a French architect's palace going up on Talcahuano, Norberto Maillart's Tribunales, and needs Italians to carve and model it. Colombo arrives contracted for exactly that: decoration on another man's building, executed to another man's line. The city he lands in is putting up more square metres a year than Milan, almost all of it in a borrowed European vocabulary, and the ministry has sent to Italy for men trained to speak it. es.wikipedia records the year, 1906, and nothing about the terms.
suggested_refs: Norberto Maillart's Palacio de Justicia, whose decorative programme brought Colombo to Argentina
sources: es.wikipedia.org, 'Palacio de Justicia de la Nación Argentina' (coordinates)

stops.name: Palacio de Justicia: copying plans with de Lázzari and Baroffio Covati
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction [R]. The whole content of this stop, the plan-copying work and the two named colleagues who crossed with him, comes from virginiocolombo.blogspot.com alone, a self-published research blog; neither Wikipedia edition mentions either man. The June date is a placeholder inside the attested arrival year and has no source behind it.
stops.campa: The work is not design. In the drafting rooms of the new Palacio de Justicia he copies plans beside Achille de Lázzari and Mario Baroffio Covati, who crossed with him and were hired for the same task. It is a clerk's apprenticeship in a foreign practice: the standards of the Argentine public works office learned by hand, line by line. De Lázzari will marry into the Giovanola family, as Colombo does; which wedding came first is not stated. One self-published blog reports both men and both marriages, and neither Wikipedia edition mentions either name.
suggested_refs: virginiocolombo.blogspot.com on Achille de Lázzari and Mario Baroffio Covati, Colombo's fellow arrivals of 1906

stops.name: Buenos Aires: director of the studio of Vinent, Maupas y Jáuregui
stops.date_confidence: Attested by es.wikipedia for the year 1909 [A], with no month and no address; the date defaults to 1 January. Neither Wikipedia edition gives the firm's office address, so the coordinate is the generic Buenos Aires city-centre pin and is not a street-level location.
stops.campa: Three years after landing he is directing the studio of the engineering firm Vinent, Maupas y Jáuregui, which puts a foreign employee in charge of the room where the firm's work is actually drawn. It has taken him three years to get out of Maillart's drafting room. No source gives the address; engineering houses of these years cluster in the blocks around the Plaza de Mayo, close to the ministries that award them work. From here he begins to sign commissions of his own rather than execute other men's.
suggested_refs: The engineering firm Vinent, Maupas y Jáuregui, whose studio Colombo directed from 1909

segments.name: The Giovanola Marriage and the Centenary

stops.name: Páez 2856, Flores: the first house he builds to live in
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia attests the address, calling it 'la primera casa que construye como vivienda en la calle Páez 2856', without a year [A for the address, R for the 1909 date]. The 1909 dating and the name Villa Raquel, along with Cesare Giovanola's role as ornamentalist, come only from virginiocolombo.blogspot.com; that the two sources describe the same building is an inference neither of them states. Páez 2856 geocodes to Flores, not to Villa Devoto as the blog implies.
stops.campa: In Flores he raises the first house he builds as a dwelling rather than as decoration on somebody else's wall, on Páez, a street of low fronts and lots still filling in. The sculptor Cesare Giovanola cuts its ornament. Giovanola's daughter, Elena Cesarina Raquel, born in La Plata in 1888, is the reason the commission is a family matter before it is a professional one. One self-published account calls the house Villa Raquel and dates it 1909. The encyclopedia that gives the address calls it only 'la primera casa que construye como vivienda'.
stops.quote: la primera casa que construye como vivienda en la calle Páez 2856
suggested_refs: The sculptor Cesare Giovanola, Colombo's father-in-law and ornamentalist

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the marriage to Elena Giovanola
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction [R] as to date and place. es.wikipedia attests the marriage, the bride's full name, her birth at La Plata on 19 November 1888, her parents Cesare Giovanola and Ángela Bossi, and the two surviving children [A]. No source reached gives the wedding's date, church or city; 'before 1909' is an inference from Giovanola's work on the Páez house and nothing more. The pin is the generic Buenos Aires centre, not an attested wedding site.
stops.campa: He marries Elena Cesarina Raquel Giovanola, the sculptor's daughter, born in La Plata on 19 November 1888 to Cesare Giovanola and Ángela Bossi. No record reached here gives the church, the date or the witnesses. Two children come of the marriage and outlive their father: Virginio, who carries the name, and María Isabel. He has married into his own trade. Cesare Giovanola cuts ornament for a living, and Colombo is about to spend twenty years putting up walls that need it, in a city where the Italian colony hires within itself.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia, 'Virginio Colombo', family section, for Elena Giovanola and the two children

stops.name: The Centenary Exposition: two pavilions and a gold medal
stops.date_confidence: es.wikipedia attests the two pavilions, Festejos y Actos Públicos and Servicio Postal, and the Gold Medal, for 1910 with no month [A]; the date defaults to 1 January. No source reached locates either pavilion, so the coordinate is the Centenary exposition ground already fixed for the Italian Pavilion at the Regimiento 1 de Patricios site and is an editorial pin, not a documented address. The unbuilt third pavilion is reported only by virginiocolombo.blogspot.com [R].
stops.campa: Argentina turns a hundred and builds an exposition scattered across the capital to say so. Colombo designs two pavilions for it, Festejos y Actos Públicos and Servicio Postal, temporary architecture meant to be admired for a season and then taken down, and wins a Gold Medal for the pair. A third pavilion he draws is never built at all. Of the postal pavilion es.wikipedia says only that it is 'aún en pie', still standing somewhere in the city, and gives no address. Standing where?
stops.quote_source: es.wikipedia.org, 'Virginio Colombo', on the Servicio Postal pavilion
suggested_refs: The Exposición Internacional del Centenario of 1910, dispersed across Barrio Norte, Palermo and the Patricios grounds

stops.name: Buenos Aires: three Italians and one style
stops.date_confidence: Attested only obliquely and with a date problem. it.wikipedia's article on Francesco Gianotti, not on Colombo, states that in the year Gianotti opened his own studio he began building Art Nouveau houses for the Argentine bourgeoisie with Palanti and Colombo; 'l'anno successivo' there follows a sentence naming both 1909 and the 1910 exposition, so the year is ambiguous between 1910 and 1911 and 1911 is an editorial reading. Neither of Colombo's own Wikipedia entries mentions the collaboration at all. Treat the year as c.1910-1911 [R], the association itself as [A].
stops.campa: He begins building Art Nouveau houses for the Argentine bourgeoisie alongside Mario Palanti and Francisco Gianotti, two other Italians working the same downtown blocks in the same years, selling a style their clients have seen in European magazines and now want in stone. The three are not a firm and not a school; they are competitors with one vocabulary and one market. The arrangement is recorded in Gianotti's Italian encyclopedia entry and in no other source reached, Colombo's own entries in either language included.
stops.quote: L'anno successivo aprì il proprio studio, e con Palanti e Virginio Colombo iniziò a realizzare edifici in stile Art Nouveau per la borghesia argentina.
suggested_refs: it.wikipedia, 'Francesco Gianotti', the only source for the three-way collaboration
Gianotti's studio at Parana 972, opened 1911

stops.name: Avenida Santa Fe 3976: the studio
stops.date_confidence: Attested by es.wikipedia's list of his professional offices, which gives the address against the year 1911 and nothing else [A]; the date defaults to 1 January. The coordinate is Avenida Santa Fe 3976 per OpenStreetMap, in Palermo Botanico.
stops.campa: His professional address in 1911 is Avenida Santa Fe 3976, north of the centre, in the blocks behind the botanical garden where the money lives. It is an address chosen to be visited by clients rather than to sit near a building site. What the studio held and how many draughtsmen worked in it, no document reached here says. es.wikipedia prints the number and the year in a list of his professional offices, with no comment beside either, and the list has two entries in it altogether.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia, 'Virginio Colombo', list of professional offices, 1911 and 1913

stops.name: Hipólito Yrigoyen 2562: the Casa Calise
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1911 by both es.wikipedia and it.wikipedia, with the address given as Hipólito Yrigoyen 2562/78, Balvanera [A]; no month, so the date defaults to 1 January. Coordinate from OpenStreetMap for Hipólito Yrigoyen 2562.
stops.campa: The Casa Calise goes up on Hipólito Yrigoyen in Balvanera, a rental block whose front is worked to the roofline like a piece of furniture: pilasters dissolving into vegetation, balconies carried on human figures, a crown of modelled stone against the sky, all of it in cement over brick and all of it for tenants rather than for a palace. It is the building cited whenever his name is cited. It is also, in plan, an ordinary Buenos Aires rental property with a light well down the middle of it.
suggested_refs: Casa Calise, Hipólito Yrigoyen 2562/78, Balvanera, the most cited of Colombo's surviving buildings

stops.name: Avenida Rivadavia 3216: the Casa de los Pavos Reales
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1912 by es.wikipedia [A], no month, date defaulted to 1 January. The address is not stable across sources: es.wikipedia's prose gives Av. Rivadavia 3216/32, its own works table gives 3222, and virginiocolombo.blogspot.com gives 3326. All three are left standing. The barrio is Balvanera, per the es.wikipedia works table and OpenStreetMap, not Almagro as some secondary accounts have it. Coordinate is OSM for Rivadavia 3216.
stops.campa: On Rivadavia he builds the house the city will name after its birds: peacocks in cement standing over the entrance, above a front that borrows Venetian Gothic windows and sets them in a liberty facade without apology. No European rule governs the mixture. The client's ambition is to have been everywhere, and one elevation is where he says so. The street number varies with the source: es.wikipedia's prose has 3216, its own works table has 3222, the blog has 3326.
suggested_refs: Casa de los Pavos Reales, Av. Rivadavia, Balvanera, and the unresolved street number

stops.name: Riobamba 358: the studio moves
stops.date_confidence: Attested by es.wikipedia's list of professional offices, which gives Riobamba 358 against 1913 [A]; no month, date defaulted to 1 January. OpenStreetMap places Riobamba 358 in Balvanera, Comuna 3, not in San Nicolás as some secondary accounts state.
stops.campa: By 1913 the office has come down from Santa Fe to Riobamba 358, in Balvanera, a short walk from the blocks where he is now building steadily. The move puts him among his own sites instead of among his clients' houses. That same year the Società Unione Operai Italiani building is inaugurated on Sarmiento, and there is work enough on Rivadavia, Corrientes and Yrigoyen to justify a man keeping his drawings closer to his bricklayers. Only two professional addresses of his are on record anywhere, this one and Santa Fe 3976, with nothing between them.
suggested_refs: es.wikipedia, 'Virginio Colombo', the two recorded studio addresses of 1911 and 1913

stops.name: Sarmiento 1374: the Società Unione Operai Italiani
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1913 by both Wikipedia editions [A]; no month, date defaulted to 1 January. The address contradicts itself within one source: es.wikipedia's prose gives Sarmiento 1374/82 and its works table gives 1364. The coordinate follows OpenStreetMap for Sarmiento 1374, San Nicolás. Bianca Schäfer's 2014 study, pp.101-131, is cited by es.wikipedia and was not independently accessed here.
stops.campa: The Italian Workers' Union Society opens its building on Sarmiento: a mutual aid body of immigrant labourers commissioning, from an immigrant architect, a headquarters as ornate as any bourgeois rental block in the city. It is the one commission of his that comes from the men who lay bricks rather than from the men who collect the rents. A century later it stands abandoned and badly deteriorated. Bianca Schäfer gives it thirty pages of study in 2014; the address in the sources is either 1364 or 1374.
suggested_refs: Bianca Schäfer, 'Società Unione Operai Italiani' (2014), pp.101-131, cited by es.wikipedia and not independently accessed

stops.name: Avenida Pueyrredón 563: the Bologna bakery
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction [R] throughout. The commission is listed only by virginiocolombo.blogspot.com, a self-published blog, and by no encyclopedia or scholarly source reached here; the blog gives no completion date at all. The 1913 date is a placeholder within his working years and carries no evidentiary weight. The coordinate is OpenStreetMap for Avenida Pueyrredón 563, Balvanera.
stops.campa: Not every commission is a facade. Somewhere in these years he decorates the inside of the Bologna bakery on Avenida Pueyrredón. One researcher's self-published blog lists the job; nothing else reached here mentions it, and the blog gives no date, no photograph and no note of what survives. This is the work that keeps a studio's lights on between buildings, and it is a shop interior: mouldings, a ceiling, wood and mirrors in a room where bread is sold across a counter.
suggested_refs: virginiocolombo.blogspot.com, sole listing of Colombo's interior-decoration commissions

stops.name: Avenida Rivadavia 2330: the Teatro Andrea Doria
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1915 by both Wikipedia editions, with the address Av. Rivadavia 2330 [A]; no month, date defaulted to 1 January. es.wikipedia's works table records the demolition in 1967. The barrio is Balvanera, not Monserrat: Monserrat lies east of Avenida Entre Ríos, which crosses Rivadavia at the 1900 numbers. Coordinate from OpenStreetMap.
stops.campa: He builds a theatre on Rivadavia and it is named for a Genoese admiral. The Italian colony of Buenos Aires now has its mutual aid society, its bakeries, its rental blocks and its stage, and Colombo has built at least one of each. The Andrea Doria stands fifty-two years. In 1967 it is pulled down, and the same year takes Villa Carú as well, so that two of his buildings leave the city within months of each other. No photograph of the interior was reached here.
suggested_refs: Teatro Andrea Doria, Av. Rivadavia 2330, demolished 1967

stops.name: Humberto 1º 2048, San Cristóbal: the Fábrica Anda
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1916 by both Wikipedia editions, address Humberto 1º 2048/60 [A]; no month, date defaulted to 1 January. The barrio is San Cristóbal per the es.wikipedia works table and OpenStreetMap, not San Telmo as some secondary accounts have it; San Telmo lies some two kilometres east of this address.
stops.campa: In San Cristóbal, at Humberto 1º 2048, he builds a factory for the Anda firm, an industrial building with an architect's front on it, in the year both encyclopedias date to 1916. The hand that models peacocks takes work from a manufacturer and puts ornament on a workshop wall. The client comes back six years later, for a house on Entre Ríos a few blocks away. Between the factory and the house sit the war years, when iron and cement are dear and Buenos Aires builds less than it would like to.
suggested_refs: Fábrica Anda, Humberto 1º 2048/60, San Cristóbal, and the later Casa Anda for the same client

stops.name: Avenida Rivadavia 5491, Caballito: Villa Carú
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1917 by es.wikipedia, whose works table reads 'Villa Carú-Costa, Av. Rivadavia 5491, Caballito, Demolida en 1967' [A]; no month, date defaulted to 1 January. Coordinate from OpenStreetMap for Av. Rivadavia 5491.
stops.campa: Further west on the same avenue, in Caballito, he builds Villa Carú for the Carú-Costa family, a detached house on a street turning into a boulevard of them. By now Rivadavia is the spine of his practice: he has built on it at the 2300 block, the 3200, the 4700 and now the 5400. The house stands fifty years, and comes down in the same year as the Andrea Doria. What the es.wikipedia works table has to say about the end of it runs to three words: 'Demolida en 1967'.
stops.quote_source: es.wikipedia.org, 'Virginio Colombo', works table entry for Villa Carú-Costa
suggested_refs: Villa Carú-Costa, Av. Rivadavia 5491, Caballito, demolished 1967

stops.name: Avenida Rivadavia 4787, Caballito: the Casa Garbesi
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1918 by es.wikipedia with the address Av. Rivadavia 4787 [A]; no month, date defaulted to 1 January. es.wikipedia records the building as demolished but gives no demolition year, which is left as a gap. Coordinate from OpenStreetMap; the barrio is Caballito.
stops.campa: The Casa Garbesi is finished at Rivadavia 4787, some blocks east of Villa Carú and a year after it. It is gone as well, and nobody troubled to write down when. es.wikipedia's works table carries the address, the year of construction and the word demolished, with no demolition date, no photograph and no description of what stood there. Most of the near fifty works are known to exactly this depth: an avenue, a number, a year, and a note on whether anything is still standing at it.
suggested_refs: Casa Garbesi, Av. Rivadavia 4787, Caballito, demolished, year unrecorded

stops.name: Avenida Corrientes 2548: the Casa Grimoldi
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1918 by both Wikipedia editions, address Av. Corrientes 2548/60 [A]; no month, date defaulted to 1 January. Coordinate from OpenStreetMap, in Balvanera, the Once district. it.wikipedia's article illustrates only two of his buildings, this one and Azcuénaga 1083-1087.
stops.campa: The Casa Grimoldi goes up at Avenida Corrientes 2548, in the Once district of Balvanera, in 1918, and unlike most of what he has built by now it survives. It is one of only two buildings the Italian encyclopedia illustrates for his entry; the other is the house on Azcuénaga. The style has cooled: less swarm on the wall, more order, the ornament arranged rather than growing out of the surface instead. Whether that is Colombo changing or the market changing, no source reached here will say.
suggested_refs: Casa Grimoldi, Av. Corrientes 2548/60, one of two Colombo buildings illustrated on it.wikipedia

stops.name: Azcuénaga 1083, Recoleta: the Lagomarsino house
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1920 by both Wikipedia editions, address Azcuénaga 1083/87, Recoleta [A]; no month, date defaulted to 1 January. Coordinate from OpenStreetMap, Barrio Norte. es.wikipedia cites casa.sanluis.gov.ar for the building's later history as the Casa de San Luis; that site was not independently accessed here.
stops.campa: In Barrio Norte he builds a house for the Lagomarsino family on Azcuénaga, the most northern and the most expensive address of his career. The front is disciplined where the Calise was luxuriant: columns behaving as columns, ornament held inside its panels. The house later passes to the province of San Luis and is known after it, kept and used and given an institutional history, which few of his buildings have. es.wikipedia cites the province's own site for that history. It was not reached here.
suggested_refs: casa.sanluis.gov.ar, institutional history of the Casa de San Luis at Azcuénaga 1083/87 (cited by es.wikipedia, not accessed)

stops.name: Avenida Entre Ríos 1081, San Cristóbal: the Casa Anda
stops.date_confidence: Attested for 1922 by es.wikipedia, whose works table reads 'Casa Anda, Av. Entre Ríos 1081, San Cristóbal, En estado de abandono y ruina' [A]; no month, date defaulted to 1 January. The barrio is San Cristóbal, not Constitución as some secondary accounts have it. Coordinate from OpenStreetMap.
stops.campa: The Anda family, for whom he built a factory six years earlier and a few blocks away, commissions a house on Entre Ríos, in the same barrio as the workshop. It is among the last of his documented works. Classicism has taken the elevation over almost entirely by now, and the modelled figures that made his name in 1911 have receded into pilasters and cornices behaving themselves. es.wikipedia's works table gives its condition as abandonment and ruin. The building is still standing.
stops.quote: En estado de abandono y ruina
stops.quote_source: es.wikipedia.org, 'Virginio Colombo', works table entry for Casa Anda
suggested_refs: Casa Anda, Av. Entre Ríos 1081, San Cristóbal, standing in ruin

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the Argentine citizenship
stops.date_confidence: The naturalization is attested by it.wikipedia, which gives no date whatever for it [A as fact, no date at all]; the 1922 shown here is a placeholder within his late career and has no source behind it. es.wikipedia does not mention the naturalization. The pin is the generic Buenos Aires centre.
stops.campa: At some point he takes Argentine nationality by naturalization. The Italian encyclopedia records the fact and nothing reached here records the year, so the moment when the Milanese who came out to copy plans becomes legally a citizen of the country he has been building is simply missing from the file. The clients whose names survive stay Italian to the end: Calise, Grimoldi, Lagomarsino, Anda, and the workers' society on Sarmiento. He changes passport and keeps the colony. es.wikipedia, which is otherwise the fuller of the two articles, does not mention the naturalization at all.
suggested_refs: it.wikipedia, 'Virginio Colombo', sole source for the naturalization, undated

stops.name: Buenos Aires: near fifty works
stops.date_confidence: Reconstruction [R] as to date; the count itself is attested. es.wikipedia's lead reads 'Realizó allí cerca de 50 obras' and its bibliography cites Aliata, Böhm, Guzmán, Ortiz and Schäfer. The 1925 date is an editorial placeholder near the end of his working life and is not sourced. The barrios named are those of the es.wikipedia works table: Balvanera, San Nicolás, Caballito, San Cristóbal and Recoleta.
stops.campa: The figure that gets repeated is close to fifty works in the city, put up in under twenty years, concentrated in Balvanera, San Nicolás, San Cristóbal, Caballito and Recoleta. Some are palaces, most are rental blocks, one is a factory and one a theatre. There is no catalogue raisonné, and no list of the fifty that two sources agree on. The literature is thin and mostly Italian: Aliata on the Buenos Aires oeuvre, Böhm, Guzmán, Ortiz, and Schäfer on the single building on Sarmiento, none of it reached here in full text.
stops.quote: uno dei più rappresentativi architetti dell'Art Nouveau in America Latina
suggested_refs: Fernando Aliata, 'Eclettismo ed arte nuova. L'opere di Virginio Colombo a Buenos Aires'
Böhm, Grementieri and Verstraeten, 'Buenos Aires. Art Nouveau'

stops.name: Moreno 2091, Balvanera: the last studio
stops.date_confidence: The address is attested by es.wikipedia only as the place of his death on 22 July 1927 [A]; no source reached says when he took the office or what he was working on there, so the January date is an editorial placeholder for the last months and is not sourced. Coordinate from OpenStreetMap for Moreno 2091, Balvanera.
stops.campa: The office is on Moreno now, in Balvanera, a few blocks from the Casa Calise and around the corner from a good part of what he has built. He is in his forties, a naturalized Argentine with a wife, two children, a father-in-law who cuts his ornament, and a manner the city is beginning to call old-fashioned. Concrete and straight lines are coming; the men who will build the nineteen-thirties are already in practice. In the record this address appears exactly once, attached to the date 22 July 1927.
suggested_refs: Moreno 2091, Balvanera, the studio where Colombo died

stops.name: Moreno 2091: the gunshot
stops.date_confidence: The date, the place and the wound are attested by es.wikipedia and the date and place independently by it.wikipedia [A]. Both editions give his age as 42; es.wikipedia's own 22 July 1884 birth date would make him 43, an internal contradiction in that article which is flagged and not resolved. The manner of death is nowhere characterised: neither suicide, accident nor homicide is stated by any source reached.
stops.campa: On 22 July 1927 he is found dead in his own studio, killed by a gunshot wound to the temporal region of the head. The encyclopedia that reports the wound reports nothing else: not who found him, not whether the weapon was his own, not whether it was suicide, accident or murder, and no note is mentioned by anyone. Nobody in the reachable literature has gone back to the police file. Both editions give his age as forty-two. es.wikipedia's own birth date, 22 July 1884, would make him forty-three, and would put his death on the day he was born.
stops.quote: falleció a la temprana edad de 42 años
suggested_refs: The 1927 Buenos Aires police and coroner records for Moreno 2091, not consulted by any reachable account

stops.name: Cementerio de la Chacarita: the burial
stops.date_confidence: The burial at the Cementerio de la Chacarita is attested by es.wikipedia [A], which gives no date for it; the day after the death is an inference and nothing more. Coordinate is the cemetery centroid per OpenStreetMap. No source reached names a grave, a section or a monument.
stops.campa: He is buried at the Chacarita, the great municipal necropolis west of the centre where the city puts most of its dead and nearly all of its immigrants. es.wikipedia records the burial and gives no date for it, no section and no grave number. Nothing reached here describes the funeral, names who attended, or says whether the workers' society on Sarmiento sent anyone. Two of his buildings will come down forty years after him, and others will go without a date being written down at all.
